title: Take out the junk
brief:
A stray debug file landed on origin. Your local main is still clean, one commit behind.

Rewriting a remote is sometimes the right call, but `--force` is blunt: it overwrites whatever origin has, even work you have never seen. `--force-with-lease` fires only when origin is exactly where your cache says it is. Fetch first so the lease is fresh, then rewrite origin back to the good commit.

goals.label: The junk commit is gone from origin's history

hints: git fetch first: the lease compares origin against your local cache of it. A stale cache means refusal.
git push --force-with-lease rewrites origin/main to your main, and refuses if anyone raced you.
